gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-devanagari: Nippo's small letters stand nearly as proud as capitals, every stroke looking cut from wire. And Noto Sans Devanagari quietly blends capitals into lowercase, keeping a compact skyline with a g open below.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-elbasan: Wire-cut strokes give Nippo its look, with lowercase nearly capital-sized. Noto Sans Elbasan brings large lowercase forms and open terminals that never pinch shut, so the whole pair feels crisp and contemporary.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic: Technical through and through, Nippo draws every stroke without thick-thin swing. Noto Sans Ethiopic adds sturdy lowercase with c terminals hanging far from the bowl, and that sturdiness is what holds the pair together.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-georgian: Nippo bends like a paperclip, every stroke one uniform line. Noto Sans Georgian meets it with open curves and short ascender stems, and that friendly openness is what the pair does best.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-glagolitic: Wire-cut and technical: Nippo gives bowls and stems the same weight, its small letters standing nearly capital-sized. Make Nippo small and Noto Sans Glagolitic simply takes over the page.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-gothic: Noto Sans Gothic has counters as big as drilled glass beads. Nippo is the spaghetti-like one, all same-width strokes up top, while the body's round forms read like open parentheses below.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Nippo never thins its curves at the shoulders, and its small letters stand almost capital-sized. Noto Sans Grantha, built from little pen-nib bowls pressed flat, starts to dominate if it grows large.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-gujarati: Nippo draws a consistently thick-only outline, wire-cut and technical, with its small letters standing almost capital-sized. Noto Sans Gujarati reads smooth, its open counters giving long paragraphs room.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-gunjala-gondi: Bent wire, basically: Nippo's round letters curl like it, small ones standing nearly capital-sized. Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi follows with crayon-thick lowercase strokes and terminals cut back to leave a wide gap.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Nippo cuts stems and curves from one gauge of tubing. It does its best work in big, brief display lines, while Noto Sans Hanunoo fills most of the height with open terminals.
